Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints

Source: R/variable_name_conformance.R
variable_name_conformance.Rd

Produces a descriptive, tidy report of names that do not conform to the SAS Version 5 transport (XPT) format naming constraints that still govern many regulatory submissions. By default a conforming name is at most eight characters long, is built only from upper-case letters, digits, and the underscore, and does not start with a digit.

Usage

variable_name_conformance(
  names,
  max_length = 8L,
  allowed_chars = "A-Z0-9_",
  allow_leading_digit = FALSE
)

Arguments

names

A character vector of names to check, or a data frame whose column names are checked. Anything else is coerced with as.character().

max_length

Maximum allowed name length, in characters. Defaults to 8L, the SAS v5 transport limit.

allowed_chars

A regular-expression character-class body describing the permitted characters (the text that would appear between [ and ]). Defaults to "A-Z0-9_": upper-case letters, digits, and the underscore. Use, for example, "A-Za-z0-9_" to also permit lower-case letters.

allow_leading_digit

Logical; when FALSE (the default) a name that begins with a digit is reported as starts_with_digit.

Value

A tibble with one row per non-conforming name per reason, and the columns:

name

The non-conforming name.

reason

One of "too_long", "invalid_character", "starts_with_digit", or "empty".

detail

A human-readable description of the finding.

When every name conforms, a zero-row tibble with the same columns is returned.

Details

Unlike the scored usability indicators (for example assess_label_quality()), this function does not score anything or emit R4SUB evidence rows; it is a purely advisory diagnostic. Every reported name may appear on more than one row when it breaks more than one rule, so the result is tidy (one row per name per reason). The following reasons are emitted:

too_long

The name is longer than max_length characters.

invalid_character

The name contains at least one character outside the set described by allowed_chars.

starts_with_digit

The first character of the name is a digit. Suppressed when allow_leading_digit = TRUE.

empty

The name is NA, empty, or white space only.

The limits are configurable so the same function can check other naming conventions (for example a longer SAS V8/V9 limit, or a case-insensitive character set). The defaults encode the documented SAS v5 rule.

See also

assess_label_quality() for the scored U-001 indicator.

Examples

# A character vector of variable names
variable_name_conformance(
  c("USUBJID", "SUBJECTID", "trt01p", "2VISIT", "AE_TERM")
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   name      reason            detail                                            
#>   <chr>     <chr>             <chr>                                             
#> 1 2VISIT    starts_with_digit name starts with a digit                          
#> 2 SUBJECTID too_long          name has 9 characters; exceeds maximum of 8       
#> 3 trt01p    invalid_character name contains characters outside the allowed set …

# Check the column names of a data frame directly
df <- data.frame(USUBJID = 1, AgeInYears = 2, check.names = FALSE)
variable_name_conformance(df)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   name       reason            detail                                           
#>   <chr>      <chr>             <chr>                                            
#> 1 AgeInYears invalid_character name contains characters outside the allowed set…
#> 2 AgeInYears too_long          name has 10 characters; exceeds maximum of 8     

# Configurable limits: allow lower case and a longer (V8) limit
variable_name_conformance(
  c("trt01p", "SUBJECTIDENTIFIER"),
  max_length = 32L,
  allowed_chars = "A-Za-z0-9_"
)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 3
#> # ℹ 3 variables: name <chr>, reason <chr>, detail <chr>
